main_text.p: חבל m. Corruptio, Perditio: Mich.2.10. Funis, Funiculus, Laqueus, Job.18.10. Eccles.12.6. בְּחֶבֶל Fune, Iosh.2.15. Metonymice, Pars, Portio hæreditatis, quæ funiculi mensorius dividebatur, Amos 7.17. Deuter.32.v.9. Iosh.17.14. Tractus, Deut.3.4. Soph.2.5. & hac significatione gen.com.est: Turba, Caterva, 1.Sam.10.5. Psal.119. v.61. Aff. חבלו Funiculus ejus, Job.18.v.10. חבלהו Vide in Kal. Plural. חבלים Funes, 2.Sam.8.2. לי חבלי נפלו Funiculi ceciderunt mihi, Psalm.16.6. id est, Possessiones peculiares: Constr. חבלי רשעים Caterva improborum, Psalm.119.61. חבלי מנשה Partes Menasse, Iosh.17. v.5. בחבלי בוץ Funibus byssinis, Esth.1. v.6. Aff. כל־חבליו Omnes funes ejus, Iesa.33.20.

חבל m. Dolor gravissimus, Tormina, quæ hominem quasi Fune arctissime constringunt, quomodo & de Doloribus parturientium usurpatur, Iesa.66.7. Plur. חבלים Dolores, Tormina, Iesa.13.8. Jerem.22.23. Constructi. וחבלי־מות Et dolores mortis, Psal.18.5. חבלי יולדה Dolores parturientis, Hos.13.13. Aff. חבליהם Dolores suos, Job.39. v.6. בחבליו In doloribus suis, Iesa.26.17.
חבל m. Pignus, Ezech.18.12. & 33.15. Fœmin. חבלה, unde cum Aff. חבלתו Pignus suum, Ezech.18.7.
חבל m. Malus, Arbor navis, à multis Funibus ei alligatis sic dicta, Prov.23.34.

חבל m. Gubernator nauticus, Nauta, Nauclerus: רב החבל Magister gubernatoris nautici, id est, Supremus nauclerus, reliquis præfectus, Jon.1.6. Plural. חבלים, Nomen baculi pastoralis, Zach.11.7.14. de cujus etymologia variant interpretes. כל חבלי הים Omnes gubernatores maris, id est, marini, Ezech.27.29. Aff. חבליך Gubernatores nautici tui, v.8.
תחבולות f. p. Solertiæ, Confilia induftria ac pru-

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points are only partly legible on the scan; points in Hebrew words are copied as far as visible and may be incomplete. The Hebrew in the first entry (e.g. בְּחֶבֶל, לי חבלי נפלו, חבלי מנשה) and in the final word may contain misreadings. The head word of the last line is a fragment continuing on the next page, and the Latin word "pru-" is hyphenated. Scan is blurred, so the Latin italic/roman distinctions are approximate. Printed "Ios." is read as "Iosh." (Josh.), "Esa." as "Iesa." (Isa.) in the abbreviations; the scan's long s was rendered as s throughout.
